title: Against Image Makers
english: Having plastered the wall with colors that had been changed, they imprinted the images upon it.
For they say, 'we make the images of the saints for their remembrance and honor.'
But those who think they are honoring the apostles in this way should learn that, instead of honoring them, they are dishonoring them even more.
From where then did bones and sinews become manifestly joined together upon the inscription of the archangel?
For Paul, having rebuked the false-named priest, spoke against the plastered wall.
For John says, 'For we know that when He is revealed, we shall be like Him…' (1 John 3:2)
translator_notes: The Greek text is cut off mid-sentence at the end: 'οταν φανερωθῇ, ομοιοι αὐτῷ'.
baehrens: PG 41-43; Tractatus contra eos qui imagines faciunt (Khazarzar) u01 open
